You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From aa8e73eed7d3084c18dd16d195748661c7e881b5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Date: Fri, 25 Mar 2022 13:30:47 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] crypto: x86/sm3 - Fixup SLS

This missed the big asm update due to being merged through the crypto
tree.

Fixes: f94909ceb1ed ("x86: Prepare asm files for straight-line-speculation")
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Signed-off-by: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>

diff --git a/arch/x86/crypto/sm3-avx-asm_64.S b/arch/x86/crypto/sm3-avx-asm_64.S
index 71e6aae23e17..b12b9efb5ec5 100644
--- a/arch/x86/crypto/sm3-avx-asm_64.S
+++ b/arch/x86/crypto/sm3-avx-asm_64.S
@@ -513,5 +513,5 @@ SYM_FUNC_START(sm3_transform_avx)
 
 	movq %rbp, %rsp;
 	popq %rbp;
-	ret;
+	RET;
 SYM_FUNC_END(sm3_transform_avx)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/crypto/sm3-avx-asm_64.S`**
   - The line containing the `ret;` instruction has been modified to `RET;`. This change is part of an update to align with the recent changes made for straight-line speculation (SLS) in assembly files.

### Relationships

- The modification in the `sm3-avx-asm_64.S` file is a fix for an oversight that occurred during a previous update related to straight-line speculation. The patch addresses a missed update that was necessary due to the file being merged through the crypto tree, ensuring that the assembly code adheres to the new specifications introduced in the earlier commit (identified by the hash `f94909ceb1ed`). This change is part of a broader effort to enhance security and performance in the x86 architecture's cryptographic functions.

1. explain how the bug occurs, including all code statements that are most likely to lead to the bug and why. 
2. explain how the bug is fixed, including code statements fixing the bug and why. 

You must include one or more code statements in point 1 and 2.
Code statements included in point 1 should be as brief as possible, only include the ones that are most related to the root cause and  the number of code statements may not exceed 3.


Here is the commit message:
crypto: x86/sm3 - Fixup SLS

This missed the big asm update due to being merged through the crypto
tree.

Fixes: f94909ceb1ed ("x86: Prepare asm files for straight-line-speculation")
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Signed-off-by: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the omission of an important update to the assembly code that was necessary for compliance with the straight-line speculation (SLS) changes. Specifically, the use of the `ret;` instruction instead of the updated `RET;` instruction could lead to improper handling of function returns, potentially exposing the system to speculative execution vulnerabilities.

Here is the patch:
 	movq %rbp, %rsp;
 	popq %rbp;
-	ret;
+	RET;
 SYM_FUNC_END(sm3_transform_avx)
--
